::: {#fig-tangent-line}

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

### R

```{r}
#| label: tangent-line-r
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   Plot of the parabola f of x equals x squared for x from -1 to 3, in blue,
#|   and the straight line s equals 2 x minus 1 in dashed vermilion. The line
#|   touches the parabola at the point (1, 1), marked by a vermilion circle,
#|   and lies below the parabola everywhere else.
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-width: 5
tl_x_ft <- seq(-1, 3, length.out = 201)
tl_curve_ft <- tibble::tibble(x = tl_x_ft, s = tl_x_ft^2)
tl_line_ft <- tibble::tibble(x = tl_x_ft, s = 2 * tl_x_ft - 1)
tl_point_ft <- tibble::tibble(x = 1, s = 1)
tl_aes_ft <- ggplot2::aes(x, s)
ggplot2::ggplot(tl_curve_ft, tl_aes_ft) +
  ggplot2::geom_line(colour = "#0072B2") +
  ggplot2::geom_line(
    data = tl_line_ft, colour = "#D55E00", linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(data = tl_point_ft, colour = "#D55E00", size = 3) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "x", y = "s")
```

### Python

```{python}
#| label: tangent-line-python
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   Plot of the parabola f of x equals x squared for x from -1 to 3, in blue,
#|   and the straight line s equals 2 x minus 1 in dashed vermilion. The line
#|   touches the parabola at the point (1, 1), marked by a vermilion circle,
#|   and lies below the parabola everywhere else.
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-width: 5
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

tl_x_ft = np.linspace(-1, 3, 201)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 4), layout="constrained")
ax.plot(tl_x_ft, tl_x_ft**2, color="#0072B2", label="f(x) = x^2")
ax.plot(tl_x_ft, 2 * tl_x_ft - 1, "--", color="#D55E00",
        label="tangent line at 1")
ax.plot(1, 1, "o", color="#D55E00", markersize=8)
ax.set_xlabel("x")
ax.set_ylabel("s")
ax.legend(loc="upper center")
plt.show()
```

:::

The [tangent line](calculus.qmd#def-tangent-line) $s = 2x - 1$ of $f(x) = x^2$ at $y = 1$ (@exm-tangent-plane).
It touches the [graph](functions.qmd#def-graph) at $(1, 1)$
and lies below it everywhere else,
as in @exm-convex-first-order.

:::
